task: Core #1186 F6-U03c: verify real PostgreSQL DDL rollback on an isolated fixture database, no Supabase access

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Critical safety unit; isolate all executing DDL in a temporary PostgreSQL service with an immutable fixture connection, explicit negative scenarios, and no cloud credentials. Failure cannot reach production or the existing Fresh Install service.

acceptanceCriteria: CI proves at least six independently injected failure stages cause an error and preserve the pre-existing fixture row and external trigger.
CI proves one positive fully committed fixture replay changes data and restores an equivalent external trigger; all checks use the actual PostgreSQL service rather than a mocked command.
Only fixed loopback connection, local fixture DB and prefixed fixture schemas can be used; incorrect host/database/users/env redirection fail before execution.
The application database and original Fresh Install workflow remain entirely unchanged, with actual provider proof still BLOCKED.
Quality tests, typecheck, build, Completion Truth and Lifecycle remain exact-head verified under existing canonical guardians.
invariants: Fixture-only SQL must mention no unprefixed public, private, auth, storage, realtime or Supabase-managed tables/schema DROP.
Rollback must retain both original user-equivalent row and managed-schema-equivalent trigger after any injected error.
A test that never reaches a genuine PostgreSQL server cannot be reported as passing the Postgres rollback proof.
The rollback workflow has no production or Supabase secrets and no automatic cloud write connection.
forbiddenStates: Any fixture test obtains a Supabase connection string from the runtime environment.
Any failed transaction commits an empty or partially recreated fixture schema.
An unexpected fixture schema, wrong DB, host or pg redirect environment selector is accepted.
A local PostgreSQL DDL rollback PASS is promoted to live 59-migration hosted readiness.

failureModes: A migration failure after DROP SCHEMA is silently continued, allowing COMMIT of partial schema.
Cross-schema trigger CASCADE deletion is not rolled back and auth-equivalent hooks remain absent.
Test command points to localhost but libpq inherited PGHOSTADDR or a service file redirects to another server.
Fixture tests pass by checking SQL text only, never exercising a running PostgreSQL service.
Connection terminates before COMMIT and old table/trigger are lost.
Fixture-only evidence is overclaimed as proof of production Supabase reset.
edgeCases: Abort BEFORE_DROP, AFTER_DROP, EARLY_DDL, LATE_DDL, BOOTSTRAP, SEED, POSTFLIGHT.
Cross-schema trigger depends on a fixture-private trigger function; DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE removes it and rollback restores it.
One successful COMMIT recreates trigger while preserving the simulated auth-schema table.
Hard command timeout and an explicit forced-client-disconnect before COMMIT.
Unexpected DB name, hostname, PGHOSTADDR, PGSERVICE, or nonlocal socket fallback.
Eventual stale GitHub artifact at previous SHA is not accepted for new branch head.

alternatives.summary: Use an isolated PostgreSQL 16 CI service and executable fixture-only rollback trials.
alternatives.reason: Demonstrates real PostgreSQL transactional DDL semantics and external trigger rollback with zero Supabase risk.

alternatives.summary: Test rollback by dropping the existing Fresh Install app schemas inside a live transaction.
alternatives.reason: Even rolled-back DDL could hold locks, affect current Auth dependencies or fail dangerously before mature independent evidence is available.

alternatives.summary: Test only regex statement ordering and mocked psql execution.
alternatives.reason: Already covered by F6-U03b; does not prove actual ROLLBACK restores state after CASCADE.

specialistReviews.finding: Even fixture-only DROP SCHEMA is unsafe when scripts read global PG connection defaults.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use fixed local fixture DB, explicit CLI args, isolated process env, loopback server identity check and never access cloud secrets.

specialistReviews.finding: Database DDL rollback must include external trigger dependencies, not just an isolated app table.
specialistReviews.resolution: Simulate Auth schema and trigger dependent on app-private function; confirm rollback and explicit positive recreation.

specialistReviews.finding: A local Postgres proof is not a Supabase Customer Baseline clean-target proof.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep separate local fixture assertion and live outstanding proof obligations; preserve manual opt-in disabled hosted path.

specialistReviews.finding: New infrastructure must not fork Fresh Install authority or bypass Control Plane evidence semantics.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep standalone isolated verification producer and document it as subordinate to existing release-proof and Completion Truth, not an independent READY gate.

challenge.scenario: Fixture runner inherits a hosted PG URL that sends destructive SQL to Supabase.
challenge.finding: An ambient env could override an otherwise localhost-looking command.
challenge.resolution: Reject PG* inherited variables and construct minimal subprocess env with fixed host/db/user/port; verify inet_server_addr, current_database and current_user before fixture SQL.

challenge.scenario: DROP SCHEMA CASCADE removes a cross-schema trigger and later SQL fails.
challenge.finding: This external dependency must be restored by transaction rollback.
challenge.resolution: Run a real PG fixture with external trigger; after failure assert old record and exact trigger function presence.

challenge.scenario: psql processes remaining commands despite an injection error.
challenge.finding: Without ON_ERROR_STOP partial replacement can be committed.
challenge.resolution: Use -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 on one connection and verify nonzero exit and complete rollback.

challenge.scenario: Only negative failures are run; success path never establishes bootstrap restoration.
challenge.finding: Rollback alone does not prove a viable committed replay.
challenge.resolution: Positive fixture transaction must commit a new app row and recreate known cross-schema trigger.

challenge.scenario: The test fixture is accidentally executed against the default postgres DB.
challenge.finding: Even prefixed objects would mutate an unintended database.
challenge.resolution: Require a dedicated fixed ephemeral database named f6_u03c_fixture and loopback host, rejecting all other strings.

challenge.scenario: A CI PASS on mocked or local-only fixtures is used as hosted Fresh Install completion evidence.
challenge.finding: Scope and proof provenance are different.
challenge.resolution: Explicitly emit LOCAL_POSTGRES_ONLY in artifacts and document outstanding target lock/credential/Storage/59-file RLS proof.

challenge.finding: Postgres should roll back connection-local transaction.
challenge.resolution: Include precommit client disconnect if possible and verify unchanged fixture rows/trigger.

challenge.scenario: Postgres container not healthy and tests accidentally skip.
challenge.finding: A skipped integration job is not real proof.
challenge.resolution: Require separate mandatory workflow job with service health and no allow-failure/continue-on-error.

proofPlan: Run exact new canonical Development Guard and Plan Before Code on full GH checkout with matching atlas ownership and 22 Known Failures.
Run pure unit tests for SQL generator and strict loopback target guard with forbidden environment overrides.
Run real Postgres16 GH service under fixed name and verify exact connected target before fixture-only DDL.
Force at least seven errors and check original fixture row + external trigger restored each time; then prove successful commit and positive trigger recreation.
Prove no database credentials or data from the hosted Supabase target are exposed to this new workflow.
Require full exact-head standard CI, TypeScript, Completion Truth and Lifecycle; keep Source/Hosted claim scope distinct.
operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The F6-U03b review compiler has an intentional abort-before-DROP barrier. The project has not yet demonstrated actual PostgreSQL DDL DROP SCHEMA CASCADE rollback, dependent cross-schema trigger recovery, or effect of failure midway through a replay. Establish an isolated, genuinely executing PostgreSQL fixture without touching any Supabase project.
observableOutcomes: An independently created, ephemeral PostgreSQL 16 service runs fixture-only rollback trials at before/after DDL, migration equivalent, trigger bootstrap, seed and postflight, and validates recovery of original data and an externally dependent trigger.
An explicit success case commits replacement fixture schemas, creates an expected new record and restores its trigger.

The runner fails closed on any target other than localhost + a fixed disposable fixture DB name, never reads real Supabase URL/secrets, never drops public/private/auth/storage/realtime schemas and never claims proof for the 59 actual migrations.
The production Fresh Install proof flow and database content remain unchanged and hosted execution stays hard-disabled.
unresolvedRisks: Local PostgreSQL rollback confirms generic transactional DDL behavior, not Supabase Auth/Storage extension-managed dependencies, RLS correctness, connection routing, or actual 59-file replay.
A real connection loss at uncertain COMMIT may require independent postflight classification; this isolated fixture can only test precommit connection interruption.
The current hosted target retains its former 0046 schema and should not be treated as clean until separately authorized, complete exact-source live verification.

in: Add one fixture-only PostgreSQL integration harness with explicit constant target and schema allowlist; assert actual destination before any fixture cleanup.
Create a GitHub Actions service postgres:16 for real rollback/failure-injection proof with no Supabase secrets, no privileged cloud connector and isolated fixture database.
Add Node/Vitest negative tests for target guards, statement order, failure injection, prohibited real schema names and non-destructive execution options.
Document exact limitations and handoff to the next genuinely controlled Supabase Fresh Install proof gate.
out: No Supabase schema write, reset, migration replay, Storage/Auth-managed modification or project state change.
No change to canonical 59-file Fresh Install workflow or removal of F6-U03b's hosted execution barrier.
No claim of full customer-baseline, cross-tenant, Alap/Pro or provider acceptance from an isolated PostgreSQL fixture.

requirements.requirement: Prove actual PostgreSQL DROP SCHEMA CASCADE rollback restores fixture data and its external trigger after multiple injected failures.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: An injected SQL error leaves a partially destroyed fixture schema.

requirements.requirement: The executable rehearsal must accept only fixed local service and fixture-prefixed schemas, without any real Supabase credentials.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A CI fixture may connect to or mutate an actual hosted Supabase database.

requirements.requirement: The isolated rollback proof must remain distinct from target schema reset, 59-file migration replay, provider-managed Storage and signed-in tenant RLS proof.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A local fixture PASS is reported as hosted Fresh Install and Office Ready.

notes: F6-U03c isolated Postgres16 rollback proof only. Generated canonical Development Guard on full checkout (run 38724728630), risk 4/5, 22 Known Failures. Permissions are strictly limited to ephemeral fixture executing SQL; no hosted project mutations or Customer Baseline readiness claim. Role entries are engineering threat-model reviews, not independently signed human endorsements.
